content:
End of June was the target to have the Preventive Maintenance Push closed out. That came and went yesterday and it is still sitting open.

Brooke started this in early May, HVAC, plumbing and electrical across the whole portfolio, and I have been the QC eye on it. I logged both cluster spot-checks as passing in late May and my read is that my part of it is finished. The crew called the HVAC run wrapped around the same time.

Before I put my name to this closing out, I need to know where every piece of it stands as of today, cluster by cluster, and I need our records saying the same thing. Work out what is actually finished and what is not, and get our tracking to match. Anything still open gets its own tracking item raised, with the person who owns that work named on it. My own spot-check records are part of that, with a short note left on each one saying where it landed and why.

Anything flagged in the field that still needs a tech back onsite belongs in our maintenance ticket log rather than sitting as a tracking item, and put a slot on my calendar to go back out and re-inspect whatever ends up in that follow-up.

Then post where this stands in the channel the push has been running in so the crew is working off the same picture, and draft an email to Brooke, cluster by cluster, with what is open, who is holding it, and what has to happen before this can close.

I do not want Brooke's email written so it can be read either way. If my QC side is a pass, say pass. If it is not, say straight out that my earlier sign-off does not hold and this should not be treated as closeable yet, with the reasons.
I will search Slack channels, Linear issues, Airtable tables, Gmail, and local files to locate
all details and tracking items for the Preventive Maintenance Push.

content: I will run a script to summarize
all Linear issues relevant to the Preventive Maintenance Push, including their state, assignee, and comments.

parameters.command:
python3 -c '
import json, urllib.request, os

# Let us query Linear issues or inspect cached outputs
import glob
files = glob.glob("/home/agent/.gemini/tmp/workspace/tool-outputs/session-*/mcp_mcp27a64177_list_issues*.txt")

issues = []
for f in files:
    with open(f) as fp:
        content = fp.read()
        try:
            data = json.loads(content)
            if "issues" in data:
                issues.extend(data["issues"])
            elif "output" in data:
                parsed = json.loads(data["output"])
                if "issues" in parsed:
                    issues.extend(parsed["issues"])
        except Exception as e:
            pass

print(f"Total issues loaded: {len(issues)}")
# Deduplicate by identifier
issue_dict = {i["identifier"]: i for i in issues if "identifier" in i}
print(f"Unique issues: {len(issue_dict)}")

pm_keywords = ["cluster", "hvac", "plumbing", "electrical", "preventive", "spot-check", "qc", "filter", "panel", "coil", "water heater", "hose bib", "condenser"]

for k, v in sorted(issue_dict.items(), key=lambda x: int(x[0].split("-")[1])):
    title = v.get("title", "")
    desc = v.get("description", "")
    state = v.get("state", {}).get("name", "")
    assignee = v.get("assignee", {}).get("name", "Unassigned") if v.get("assignee") else "Unassigned"
    proj = v.get("project", {}).get("id", "") if v.get("project") else ""
    
    # check relevance
    combined = (title + " " + desc).lower()
    if any(kw in combined for kw in pm_keywords) or proj == "proj_003":
        print(f"{k}: [{state}] (Proj: {proj}, Assignee: {assignee}) - {title}")
'

able's Maintenance Tickets table to avoid ID collisions.

parameters.command:
python3 -c '
import json, glob

files = glob.glob("/home/agent/.gemini/tmp/workspace/tool-outputs/session-*/mcp_mcp27a64177_list_records_for_table*.txt")

for f in files:
    with open(f) as fp:
        try:
            data = json.loads(fp.read())
            recs = data.get("records", [])
            for r in recs:
                fields = r.get("fields", {})
                tn = fields.get("Ticket Number")
                comp = fields.get("Completion Date")
                desc = fields.get("Description", "")[:80]
                if tn:
                    print(f"Ticket: {tn} | Completion: {comp} | Desc: {desc}")
        except Exception as e:
            pass
'

**Preventive Maintenance Push — Portfolio Status Update (As of July 1, 2026)**

Team, here is where every piece of the Preventive Maintenance Push stands across all four clusters following today's records audit:

1. **North Cluster**: **COMPLETE**. All HVAC, plumbing, and electrical servicing verified and signed off via QC spot-check.
2. **East Cluster**: **COMPLETE**. All HVAC coil servicing and filter checks completed by Elias and verified via QC.

- My late-May spot-check sign-off was specific to the HVAC sweep and does not apply to overall PM Push closeout while field repairs and West Cluster items remain pending.
- I have scheduled a field re-inspection block for **Monday, July 6 from 9:00 AM – 12:00 PM** to walk the South Cluster plumbing repairs once completed.
- Full PM Push closeout is held until tech field repairs are complete, West Cluster scope is wrapped, and final QC re-inspection is signed off.

parameters.body:
Hi Brooke,

I have completed a thorough cluster-by-cluster audit of the Preventive Maintenance Push as of today (July 1, 2026) and aligned our internal tracking systems across Linear and Airtable.

I am writing to state clearly and unequivocally: My earlier QC spot-check sign-off from late May applied only to the initial HVAC run and DOES NOT HOLD for the overall Preventive Maintenance Push. On the Quality Control side, this push is NOT a pass, and it should NOT be treated as closeable yet.

Below is the exact status of each cluster, what remains open, who owns each piece, and what must occur before we can formally close out the push:

---

1. SOUTH CLUSTER
- Status: HVAC & Electrical complete; Plumbing field repairs OPEN.
- Open Work: Carlos Mendez's plumbing audit flagged two water heaters requiring full replacement and a series of exterior hose bib repairs. Because these field issues require a tech back onsite, they have been transferred out of tracking into active Airtable Maintenance Tickets: MT-2026-1327 (Water Heater #1), MT-2026-1328 (Water Heater #2), and MT-2026-1329 (Hose Bib Repairs).
- Owner: Carlos Mendez (Linear tracking issue: OPS-1000).
- Action Required: Tech dispatch and physical completion of water heater replacements and hose bib repairs.

2. NORTH CLUSTER
- Status: COMPLETE.
- Summary: All HVAC coil cleanings, filter swaps, and PM audit items completed by Tony Reyes and Wesley Tran. Spot-checks passed. Tracking updated (OPS-44, OPS-87, OPS-98 marked Done).
- Open Work: None.

3. EAST CLUSTER
- Status: COMPLETE.
- Summary: HVAC coil cleanings and filter checks completed by Elias Navarro. Spot-checks passed. Tracking updated (OPS-99, OPS-108 marked Done).
- Open Work: None.

4. WEST CLUSTER
- Status: IN PROGRESS / OPEN.
- Open Work: Finalizing remaining PM push audit scope, vendor coordination, and field completion across West Cluster properties.
- Owner: Lisa Smith (onsite lead) and John Smith (maintenance lead) (Linear tracking issue: OPS-1001).
- Action Required: Completion of remaining cluster PM work orders and final walkthrough submission.

5. PORTFOLIO QC RE-INSPECTION & CLOSEOUT
- Status: IN PROGRESS / OPEN.
- Owner: Jaime Salinas (Linear tracking issue: OPS-1002).
- Action Required: I have reserved Monday, July 6, 2026, from 9:00 AM to 12:00 PM on my calendar to conduct field re-inspections of the South Cluster plumbing repairs once Carlos's techs complete the work.

---

SUMMARY OF CLOSEOUT PREREQUISITES:
Before the Preventive Maintenance Push can be closed:
1. Carlos Mendez must complete tech execution for South Cluster plumbing work order tickets MT-2026-1327, MT-2026-1328, and MT-2026-1329.
2. Lisa Smith must finalize and sign off on West Cluster PM push items under OPS-1001.
3. I must perform the July 6 field re-inspection and issue a formal, portfolio-wide QC pass.

Let me know if you have any questions or need further breakdown.

Best regards,

Jaime Salinas
Quality Control Inspector
Star Property Management
